h1.en: Just Lost Your Job in Alabama? Here Are Your Health Insurance Options for 2026
h1.es: Acaba de Perder Su Trabajo en Alabama? Estas Son Sus Opciones de Seguro Medico 2026

subhero.en: You have 60 days from your last day of employer coverage to enroll in a new plan. Alabama did not expand Medicaid under the ACA, so most laid-off workers in Alabama will use a Marketplace Special Enrollment Period at healthcare.gov, not the state Medicaid program.
subhero.es: Tiene 60 dias desde su ultimo dia de cobertura del empleador para inscribirse. Alabama no expanded Medicaid bajo el ACA, por lo que la mayoria de trabajadores despedidos usaran el Mercado federal en healthcare.gov.

heading.en: You have 60 days from your Alabama coverage loss date
heading.es: Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura en Alabama

body.en: Your 60-day loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period starts the day after your employer coverage ends in Alabama. For example, if your last day of Alabama employer coverage is July 31, 2026, your SEP window runs August 1 through September 29, 2026. Miss that window and you typically wait until the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026, for coverage beginning January 1, 2027. Alabama Medicaid has extremely strict eligibility for working-age adults who are not pregnant, parenting, or disabled, so the Marketplace SEP is the primary path for most Alabama job-loss situations.
body.es: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias por perdida de cobertura comienza el dia despues de que termina su cobertura del empleador en Alabama. Por ejemplo, si su ultimo dia de cobertura es el 31 de julio de 2026, su ventana SEP corre del 1 de agosto al 29 de septiembre de 2026. Si pierde esa ventana, tipicamente espera hasta la Inscripcion Abierta ACA 2027 que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026 para cobertura del 1 de enero de 2027. Alabama Medicaid tiene elegibilidad muy estricta para adultos en edad laboral que no son embarazadas, padres o discapacitados.

quickAnswer.en: Losing job-based health insurance in Alabama triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period (SEP) under federal HIPAA rules. Alabama is a non-expansion state, so most working-age adults who lose a job do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid unless they are pregnant, parenting a minor child, or have a qualifying disability. Your primary options in 2026 are: (1) ACA Marketplace plan at healthcare.gov with income-based premium tax credits, typically $10 to $300 per month after subsidies if your projected 2026 income falls between 100% and 400% FPL; (2) COBRA continuation at 102% of the full premium, often $500 to $2,000 per month; or (3) your spouse's employer plan if you are married, with a 30-day enrollment window. Children in the household may qualify for ALL Kids, Alabama's CHIP program, year-round regardless of Medicaid expansion status.
quickAnswer.es: Perder el seguro medico del trabajo en Alabama activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) de 60 dias bajo las reglas federales de HIPAA. Alabama es un estado sin expansion de Medicaid, por lo que la mayoria de adultos en edad laboral que pierden un trabajo no califican para Alabama Medicaid a menos que sean embarazadas, padres de menores, o tengan una discapacidad calificada. Sus opciones principales en 2026 son: (1) plan del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov con creditos fiscales basados en ingresos, tipicamente $10 a $300 al mes despues de subsidios; (2) continuacion COBRA al 102% de la prima completa, a menudo $500 a $2,000 al mes; o (3) el plan del empleador del conyuge, con ventana de 30 dias. Los ninos pueden calificar para ALL Kids, el programa CHIP de Alabama, todo el ano.

introParagraphs.en: Losing a job in Alabama means confronting a health insurance gap in a state with one of the most restrictive Medicaid programs in the country. Alabama did not expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act and remains one of 10 non-expansion states as of 2026. For working-age adults who are not pregnant, parenting a minor child, or receiving a qualifying disability determination, Alabama Medicaid eligibility is limited to very low income levels, typically well under 20% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). That means most people laid off in Alabama will not find a Medicaid lifeline waiting for them. What is available is the federal loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period (SEP) under HIPAA Section 9831, which opens a 60-day window to enroll in an ACA Marketplace plan at healthcare.gov after losing employer coverage. Alabama residents who lose their jobs and whose projected 2026 income falls between 100% FPL ($15,060 for a single person) and 400% FPL ($63,840 for a single person) qualify for premium tax credits that significantly reduce Marketplace plan costs. The 2026 ACA Open Enrollment Period ended January 15, 2026. Without acting on the SEP before Day 60, most Alabamians who lose a job will have no subsidized coverage path until the 2027 Open Enrollment Period begins November 1, 2026.
introParagraphs.es: Perder un trabajo en Alabama significa enfrentar una brecha de seguro medico en un estado con uno de los programas de Medicaid mas restrictivos del pais. Alabama no expanded Medicaid bajo la Ley de Cuidado Asequible y sigue siendo uno de los 10 estados sin expansion a partir de 2026. Para adultos en edad laboral que no son embarazadas, padres de menores o que reciben una determinacion de discapacidad calificada, la elegibilidad de Alabama Medicaid esta limitada a niveles de ingresos muy bajos, tipicamente bien por debajo del 20% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza (FPL). Eso significa que la mayoria de personas despedidas en Alabama no encontraran un salvavidas de Medicaid esperandolas. Lo que si esta disponible es el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) federal por perdida de cobertura bajo la Seccion 9831 de HIPAA, que abre una ventana de 60 dias para inscribirse en un plan del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov despues de perder la cobertura del empleador.

introParagraphs.en: Alabama residents navigating job loss in 2026 face a specific policy environment that shapes their options. First, Alabama has a coverage gap for adults with very low incomes: those who project annual income below 100% FPL ($15,060 for a single person) neither qualify for Alabama Medicaid nor qualify for ACA Marketplace premium tax credits, because Marketplace subsidies begin at 100% FPL on the assumption that expansion Medicaid covers those below that line. Second, Alabama uses the federal healthcare.gov Marketplace rather than a state-based exchange, so all Marketplace applications run through healthcare.gov. Third, Alabama's ALL Kids program (the state CHIP program) covers children regardless of the Medicaid expansion gap, providing a critical safety net for children in job-loss households. Fourth, COBRA continuation under federal rules applies to employers with 20 or more employees, charging 102% of the full group premium; smaller Alabama employers may not be subject to federal COBRA, though Alabama does not maintain a mini-COBRA statute. Understanding these four factors is essential before choosing a coverage path after job loss in Alabama in 2026.
introParagraphs.es: Los residentes de Alabama que navegan la perdida de trabajo en 2026 enfrentan un entorno de politica especifico que moldea sus opciones. Primero, Alabama tiene una brecha de cobertura para adultos con ingresos muy bajos: aquellos que proyectan ingresos anuales por debajo del 100% FPL ($15,060 para una persona) ni califican para Alabama Medicaid ni para los creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado ACA. Segundo, Alabama usa el Mercado federal healthcare.gov en lugar de un intercambio estatal. Tercero, el programa ALL Kids de Alabama (el programa CHIP estatal) cubre ninos independientemente de la brecha de expansion de Medicaid. Cuarto, la continuacion COBRA bajo reglas federales se aplica a empleadores con 20 o mas empleados, cobrando el 102% de la prima grupal completa. Comprender estos cuatro factores es esencial antes de elegir un camino de cobertura despues de perder el trabajo en Alabama en 2026.

name.en: Confirm your last day of Alabama employer coverage
name.es: Confirme su ultimo dia de cobertura del empleador en Alabama

text.en: Call your Alabama employer's HR department or review your termination letter to get the exact date your employer health coverage ends. Most Alabama employer plans end on the last day of the month you are terminated, but some end on the actual termination date. This date starts your 60-day SEP clock. Request a HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage in writing immediately, as you will need it as proof of the qualifying life event when you submit your Marketplace SEP application at healthcare.gov.
text.es: Llame al departamento de recursos humanos de su empleador en Alabama o revise su carta de terminacion para obtener la fecha exacta en que termina la cobertura. La mayoria de planes del empleador en Alabama terminan el ultimo dia del mes en que fue despedido. Esta fecha inicia su reloj SEP de 60 dias. Solicite un certificado de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA por escrito de inmediato, ya que lo necesitara como prueba del evento calificador de vida cuando envie su solicitud SEP del Mercado en healthcare.gov.

name.en: Calculate your projected 2026 household income for subsidy eligibility
name.es: Calcule su ingreso proyectado del hogar 2026 para elegibilidad de subsidio

text.en: Alabama ACA Marketplace subsidies use Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) based on what you expect to earn for the rest of 2026, not your former salary. Include unemployment compensation in your projection (unemployment benefits count as income for ACA subsidy purposes under IRS rules). For 2026, the 138% FPL threshold in Alabama is $22,025 for a single person and $45,540 for a family of four. Because Alabama did not expand Medicaid, the critical Marketplace threshold is 100% FPL ($15,060 single, $31,200 family of 4): households projecting income below that level are in the Alabama coverage gap and cannot access Marketplace subsidies. Households projecting income between 100% and 400% FPL ($63,840 single) qualify for premium tax credits.
text.es: Los subsidios del Mercado ACA de Alabama usan el Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) basado en lo que espera ganar el resto de 2026, no su salario anterior. Incluya la compensacion por desempleo en su proyeccion. Para 2026, el umbral de 100% FPL en Alabama es $15,060 para una persona y $31,200 para una familia de cuatro. Porque Alabama no expanded Medicaid, el umbral critico del Mercado es el 100% FPL: hogares que proyectan ingresos por debajo de ese nivel estan en la brecha de cobertura de Alabama y no pueden acceder a subsidios del Mercado. Hogares que proyectan entre 100% y 400% FPL ($63,840 individual) califican para creditos fiscales de prima.

name.en: Check Alabama Medicaid eligibility if you are pregnant, parenting, or disabled
name.es: Verifique elegibilidad de Alabama Medicaid si es embarazada, padre o discapacitado

text.en: Alabama Medicaid covers pregnant women at higher income levels, parents with minor children at very low income thresholds (typically under 18% FPL for parents), and adults with qualifying disabilities. If you or a family member falls in one of those categories after job loss, apply through the Alabama Medicaid Agency at medicaid.alabama.gov. Alabama Medicaid enrollment is open year-round for eligible categories. If you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid under the state's restricted eligibility rules, proceed directly to the ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov.
text.es: Alabama Medicaid cubre mujeres embarazadas a niveles de ingresos mas altos, padres con hijos menores a umbrales de ingresos muy bajos (tipicamente bajo el 18% FPL para padres), y adultos con discapacidades calificadas. Si usted o un miembro de la familia cae en una de esas categorias despues de perder el trabajo, solicite a traves de la Agencia de Medicaid de Alabama en medicaid.alabama.gov. La inscripcion de Alabama Medicaid es abierta todo el ano para categorias elegibles. Si no califica bajo las reglas restrictivas del estado, proceda directamente al SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov.

name.en: Apply for ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov within 60 days
name.es: Solicite el SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov dentro de 60 dias

text.en: Log in to healthcare.gov and select 'Report a life event,' then select 'Lost health insurance through a job.' Upload your termination letter or HIPAA certificate as documentation of the qualifying life event. Compare Silver and Gold plan options for your Alabama ZIP code. In 2026, premium tax credits reduce most Silver plans to $10 to $300 per month for applicants with projected income between 100% and 400% FPL. Alabama uses the federal healthcare.gov platform, not a state-based exchange, so all Alabama Marketplace applications and plan comparisons happen at healthcare.gov. Your new plan typically takes effect on the first of the month following enrollment.
text.es: Inicie sesion en healthcare.gov y seleccione 'Reportar un evento de vida,' luego 'Perdi el seguro medico a traves de un trabajo.' Suba su carta de terminacion o certificado HIPAA como documentacion del evento calificador de vida. Compare opciones de planes Silver y Gold para su codigo postal en Alabama. En 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima reducen la mayoria de planes Silver a $10 a $300 al mes para solicitantes con ingreso proyectado entre 100% y 400% FPL. Alabama usa la plataforma federal healthcare.gov, no un intercambio estatal, por lo que todas las solicitudes y comparaciones del Mercado de Alabama ocurren en healthcare.gov. Su nuevo plan tipicamente entra en vigor el primero del mes siguiente a la inscripcion.

name.en: Check whether your spouse's employer plan is an option
name.es: Verifique si el plan del empleador de su conyuge es una opcion

text.en: Your Alabama job loss is also a qualifying life event for your spouse's employer plan, giving your spouse's HR department 30 days to add you. Call your spouse's HR immediately, because the 30-day employer-plan window is separate from and shorter than the 60-day Marketplace SEP. Compare the employer plan's premium cost and provider network against Marketplace options at healthcare.gov for your Alabama ZIP code before committing. Your spouse's employer plan is often the cheapest option if the premium is employer-subsidized and the network includes your existing Alabama providers.
text.es: La perdida de trabajo en Alabama es tambien un evento calificador de vida para el plan del empleador de su conyuge, dandole 30 dias para inscribirse. Llame inmediatamente a los recursos humanos de su conyuge, porque la ventana de 30 dias del plan del empleador es separada y mas corta que el SEP del Mercado de 60 dias. Compare el costo de prima del plan del empleador y la red de proveedores contra las opciones del Mercado en healthcare.gov para su codigo postal en Alabama antes de comprometerse.

name.en: Evaluate COBRA only after comparing all Alabama Marketplace options
name.es: Evalue COBRA solo despues de comparar todas las opciones del Mercado de Alabama

text.en: COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium (employer share plus employee share plus 2% administrative fee). For an Alabama individual plan, COBRA typically runs $500 to $900 per month; for family coverage, $1,200 to $2,800 per month in 2026. Federal COBRA applies only if your Alabama employer had 20 or more employees. COBRA is worth evaluating only if you have ongoing treatment with an Alabama specialist not in any Marketplace network, or if your 2026 deductible is already substantially met and you need to maintain your current plan through year-end. You have 60 days to elect COBRA retroactively, so you do not need to decide on Day 1, but do compare healthcare.gov Marketplace costs before the window closes.
text.es: COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa (parte del empleador mas la del empleado mas el 2% de tarifa administrativa). Para un plan individual en Alabama, COBRA tipicamente alcanza $500 a $900 al mes; para cobertura familiar, $1,200 a $2,800 al mes en 2026. El COBRA federal aplica solo si su empleador en Alabama tenia 20 o mas empleados. COBRA vale la pena evaluar solo si tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista de Alabama que no esta en ninguna red del Mercado, o si su deducible de 2026 ya esta sustancialmente cumplido. Tiene 60 dias para elegir COBRA retroactivamente.

name.en: Check ALL Kids for your children even if you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid
name.es: Verifique ALL Kids para sus hijos aunque no califique para Alabama Medicaid

text.en: ALL Kids is Alabama's CHIP program and covers children regardless of the Medicaid expansion gap. ALL Kids eligibility extends to children up to age 19 in households with income up to 312% FPL (roughly $86,000 for a family of four in 2026), depending on coverage tier. ALL Kids enrollment is year-round with no deadline. Even if you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid yourself after job loss, your children may qualify for ALL Kids at low or zero cost. Apply through the Alabama Medicaid Agency at medicaid.alabama.gov or through healthcare.gov, which routes CHIP applications to the appropriate state program.
text.es: ALL Kids es el programa CHIP de Alabama y cubre a ninos independientemente de la brecha de expansion de Medicaid. La elegibilidad de ALL Kids se extiende a ninos hasta los 19 anos en hogares con ingresos hasta el 312% FPL (aproximadamente $86,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026), dependiendo del nivel de cobertura. La inscripcion de ALL Kids es todo el ano sin fecha limite. Incluso si no califica para Alabama Medicaid despues de perder el trabajo, sus hijos pueden calificar para ALL Kids a bajo costo o sin costo. Solicite a traves de la Agencia de Medicaid de Alabama en medicaid.alabama.gov o a traves de healthcare.gov.

intro.en: The costliest mistakes Alabama residents make after losing job-based coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que los residentes de Alabama cometen despues de perder cobertura del trabajo en 2026:

items.en: Assuming Alabama Medicaid will cover them after job loss. Alabama is a non-expansion state. Most working-age adults without qualifying children, pregnancy, or disability do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid regardless of income level. Apply at healthcare.gov for Marketplace coverage, not just medicaid.alabama.gov.
items.es: Asumir que Alabama Medicaid los cubrira despues de perder el trabajo. Alabama es un estado sin expansion. La mayoria de adultos en edad laboral sin hijos calificados, embarazo o discapacidad no califican para Alabama Medicaid. Solicite en healthcare.gov para cobertura del Mercado.

items.en: Defaulting to COBRA without comparing Alabama Marketplace options. COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium, typically $500 to $2,800 per month. ACA Marketplace plans with premium tax credits at healthcare.gov typically cost $10 to $300 per month for moderate-income applicants in 2026.
items.es: Optar automaticamente por COBRA sin comparar las opciones del Mercado de Alabama. COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa, tipicamente $500 a $2,800 al mes. Los planes del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales tipicamente cuestan $10 a $300 al mes para solicitantes de ingresos moderados en 2026.

items.en: Reporting your old Alabama salary instead of projected 2026 income. The Marketplace calculates premium tax credits on Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for the remainder of 2026, not your former salary. A lower projected income means a larger premium tax credit and potentially a cost-sharing reduction plan.
items.es: Reportar su salario antiguo en Alabama en lugar del ingreso proyectado de 2026. El Mercado calcula los creditos fiscales de prima sobre el Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) para el resto de 2026, no su salario anterior. Un ingreso proyectado menor significa un credito fiscal de prima mayor.

items.en: Missing the 60-day Alabama Marketplace SEP window. Healthcare.gov will reject a SEP application submitted after Day 60 without documentation of a second qualifying life event. The next subsidized coverage option is the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026.
items.es: Perder la ventana SEP de 60 dias del Mercado de Alabama. Healthcare.gov rechazara una solicitud SEP enviada despues del dia 60 sin documentacion de un segundo evento calificador de vida. La proxima opcion de cobertura subsidiada es la Inscripcion Abierta ACA 2027 que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026.

items.en: Forgetting to check ALL Kids for children. Alabama's CHIP program ALL Kids covers children up to 312% FPL year-round regardless of Medicaid expansion status. Even if you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid, your children may get free or low-cost comprehensive coverage through ALL Kids.
items.es: Olvidar verificar ALL Kids para los ninos. El programa CHIP de Alabama ALL Kids cubre ninos hasta el 312% FPL todo el ano independientemente del estado de expansion de Medicaid. Aunque no califique para Alabama Medicaid, sus hijos pueden obtener cobertura integral gratuita o de bajo costo a traves de ALL Kids.

items.en: Forgetting that unemployment compensation counts as income for ACA subsidy calculations. Include your weekly Alabama unemployment benefit times the number of weeks you expect to receive it in your projected 2026 annual income when applying at healthcare.gov. Undercounting income and later correcting it can shift you from Marketplace subsidies to a coverage gap at the 100% FPL line.
items.es: Olvidar que la compensacion por desempleo cuenta como ingreso para los calculos de subsidio ACA. Incluya su beneficio semanal de desempleo de Alabama multiplicado por el numero de semanas que espera recibirlo en su ingreso anual proyectado de 2026 al solicitar en healthcare.gov. Subestimar los ingresos puede desplazarlo desde subsidios del Mercado hacia la brecha de cobertura al 100% FPL.

heading.en: COBRA vs Marketplace vs Spouse's Plan in Alabama: Which Should You Choose in 2026?
heading.es: COBRA vs Mercado vs Plan del Conyuge en Alabama: Cual Debe Elegir en 2026?

body.en: After losing job-based coverage in Alabama in 2026, three primary pathways open for most adults. COBRA preserves your old Alabama employer plan at 102% of the full group premium, typically $500 to $900 per month for an individual and $1,200 to $2,800 per month for family coverage, making it the most expensive option in nearly every scenario. ACA Marketplace plans at healthcare.gov reduce most enrollees to $10 to $300 per month after premium tax credits in 2026, per the KFF Marketplace Premium Analysis, with the trade-off that you may need to change providers if your former Alabama employer's network differs from available Marketplace plan networks in your county. A spouse's employer plan costs the employee's share of the group premium, often $100 to $600 per month, and is available if your spouse's employer offers a qualifying-event SEP of 30 days, which most do under Section 9831 of HIPAA. Alabama Medicaid is not a realistic option for most working-age adults who lose jobs in Alabama: the state's non-expansion status restricts adult eligibility to pregnant women, parents of minor children at very low income thresholds, and adults with qualifying disabilities. The decision framework for Alabama job-loss situations in 2026 is: (1) check Alabama Medicaid only if you are pregnant, parenting at very low income, or disabled; (2) check ALL Kids for any children under age 19; (3) check your spouse's employer plan if married and if the premium and network are acceptable; (4) apply for ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov with premium tax credits (the main 2026 path for most Alabama job-loss situations); (5) use COBRA only as a last resort for ongoing specialist treatment or a substantially met deductible.
body.es: Despues de perder la cobertura del trabajo en Alabama en 2026, tres caminos principales se abren para la mayoria de los adultos. COBRA preserva su plan anterior del empleador de Alabama al 102% de la prima grupal completa, tipicamente $500 a $900 al mes para un individuo y $1,200 a $2,800 al mes para cobertura familiar, convirtiendolo en la opcion mas cara en casi todos los escenarios. Los planes del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov reducen a la mayoria de inscritos a $10 a $300 al mes despues de creditos fiscales de prima en 2026. El plan del empleador del conyuge cuesta la parte del empleado de la prima grupal, a menudo $100 a $600 al mes, disponible si el empleador ofrece un SEP de evento calificador de 30 dias. Alabama Medicaid no es una opcion realista para la mayoria de adultos en edad laboral que pierden empleos en Alabama: el estatus de no expansion del estado restringe la elegibilidad adulta a mujeres embarazadas, padres de menores a umbrales de ingresos muy bajos, y adultos con discapacidades calificadas. El marco de decision: primero verificar Alabama Medicaid solo si es embarazada, padre a ingresos muy bajos o discapacitado; segundo verificar ALL Kids para ninos menores de 19; tercero el plan del conyuge si es casado; cuarto solicitar SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov; quinto usar COBRA solo como ultimo recurso.

es.footnote: En Alabama (estado sin expansion), el umbral critico del Mercado es el 100% FPL (no el 138% FPL). Adultos que proyectan ingresos por debajo del 100% FPL no califican para Alabama Medicaid como adultos en edad laboral no discapacitados, y no califican para subsidios del Mercado, creando la brecha de cobertura de Alabama. El precipicio de subsidio del 400% FPL regreso para 2026 despues de que los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados de ARPA e IRA expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026.

heading.en: Alabama's Coverage Gap: Why Medicaid Does Not Help Most Job-Loss Situations in 2026
heading.es: La Brecha de Cobertura de Alabama: Por Que Medicaid No Ayuda a la Mayoria de Perdidas de Trabajo en 2026

paragraphs.en: Alabama Medicaid operates under pre-ACA rules for working-age adults. Alabama chose not to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act and remains a non-expansion state in 2026. Under Alabama's restricted eligibility framework, working-age adults without minor children, without a qualifying pregnancy, or without a Social Security Administration disability determination are not eligible for Alabama Medicaid regardless of income level. That means an Alabama resident who loses a job and has zero income may still not qualify for Alabama Medicaid if they are a non-parenting adult without a disability determination. This is the Alabama coverage gap: adults whose income falls below 100% FPL ($15,060 for a single person in 2026) are stuck between ineligibility for Alabama Medicaid and ineligibility for Marketplace premium tax credits, which start at 100% FPL on the assumption that expansion Medicaid covers those below that line.
paragraphs.es: Alabama Medicaid opera bajo reglas pre-ACA para adultos en edad laboral. Alabama eligio no expandir Medicaid bajo la Ley de Cuidado Asequible y sigue siendo un estado sin expansion en 2026. Bajo el marco de elegibilidad restringido de Alabama, adultos en edad laboral sin hijos menores, sin un embarazo calificado, o sin una determinacion de discapacidad de la Administracion de Seguridad Social no son elegibles para Alabama Medicaid independientemente del nivel de ingresos. Eso significa que un residente de Alabama que pierde un trabajo y tiene cero ingresos puede aun no calificar para Alabama Medicaid si es un adulto sin hijos sin una determinacion de discapacidad. Esta es la brecha de cobertura de Alabama: adultos cuyo ingreso cae por debajo del 100% FPL ($15,060 para una persona en 2026) quedan atrapados entre la inelegibilidad para Alabama Medicaid y la inelegibilidad para creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado.

paragraphs.en: Alabama Medicaid does cover certain categories at higher income levels. Pregnant women in Alabama qualify for Medicaid at up to 211% FPL through PeachState or the Alabama Medicaid Agency, receiving full coverage during pregnancy and for 60 days postpartum. Parents with dependent minor children qualify at very low income levels, typically under 18% FPL for a household of three. Adults with a qualifying disability determination from the Social Security Administration may qualify for both Medicaid and Medicare depending on the nature and duration of the disability. Seniors aged 65 and older qualify for Medicare as the primary payer, with Alabama Medicaid as a possible secondary payer for dual-eligible individuals with very low income. For most working-age adults who lose a job in Alabama without one of these qualifying categories, the ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov is the primary and often only subsidized coverage option.
paragraphs.es: Alabama Medicaid si cubre ciertas categorias a niveles de ingresos mas altos. Mujeres embarazadas en Alabama califican para Medicaid hasta el 211% FPL a traves de la Agencia de Medicaid de Alabama, recibiendo cobertura completa durante el embarazo y por 60 dias posparto. Los padres con hijos menores dependientes califican a niveles de ingresos muy bajos, tipicamente bajo el 18% FPL para un hogar de tres. Adultos con una determinacion de discapacidad calificada de la Administracion de Seguridad Social pueden calificar para Medicaid y Medicare. Para la mayoria de adultos en edad laboral que pierden un trabajo en Alabama sin una de estas categorias calificadas, el SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov es la opcion de cobertura subsidiada principal y a menudo unica.

heading.en: ALL Kids: Alabama's CHIP Program for Children After Job Loss in 2026
heading.es: ALL Kids: El Programa CHIP de Alabama para Ninos Despues de Perder el Trabajo en 2026

paragraphs.en: ALL Kids is Alabama's Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) and provides comprehensive health coverage for children up to age 19 whose families do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid. ALL Kids eligibility in Alabama extends up to 312% of the Federal Poverty Level, which is roughly $101,000 for a family of four in 2026. ALL Kids covers doctor visits, hospital care, prescription drugs, dental care, and vision coverage. Enrollment is open year-round with no deadline, making ALL Kids a critical safety net for children in households affected by job loss. Even if a parent's projected 2026 income falls in the Alabama coverage gap (below 100% FPL) or is too high for Alabama Medicaid but below 312% FPL, children in the household may qualify for ALL Kids at low or no cost.
paragraphs.es: ALL Kids es el Programa de Seguro de Salud para Ninos (CHIP) de Alabama y proporciona cobertura medica integral para ninos hasta los 19 anos cuyas familias no califican para Alabama Medicaid. La elegibilidad de ALL Kids en Alabama se extiende hasta el 312% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza, que es aproximadamente $101,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026. ALL Kids cubre visitas medicas, atencion hospitalaria, medicamentos recetados, atencion dental y cobertura de vision. La inscripcion es abierta todo el ano sin fecha limite, haciendo de ALL Kids una red de seguridad critica para ninos en hogares afectados por la perdida de trabajo.

paragraphs.en: ALL Kids has three coverage tiers based on income. ALL Kids I covers children in families from 0% to 100% FPL (those who do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid for children) with no premium and minimal cost-sharing. ALL Kids II covers families from 100% to 200% FPL with a modest monthly premium and small copays. ALL Kids III covers families from 200% to 312% FPL with a higher monthly premium but still far below commercial insurance rates. Apply for ALL Kids at medicaid.alabama.gov or through healthcare.gov, which routes CHIP applications to the appropriate Alabama agency. A parent who applies for their own Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov should simultaneously apply their children for ALL Kids through the same application process, as healthcare.gov automatically screens for CHIP eligibility.
paragraphs.es: ALL Kids tiene tres niveles de cobertura basados en ingresos. ALL Kids I cubre ninos en familias del 0% al 100% FPL con cero prima y costos compartidos minimos. ALL Kids II cubre familias del 100% al 200% FPL con una prima mensual modesta y pequenos copagos. ALL Kids III cubre familias del 200% al 312% FPL con una prima mensual mas alta pero aun muy por debajo de las tasas de seguro comercial. Solicite ALL Kids en medicaid.alabama.gov o a traves de healthcare.gov, que enruta solicitudes CHIP a la agencia de Alabama correspondiente.

heading.en: Documents and Proof: What Alabama Job-Loss SEP Applications Require
heading.es: Documentos y Pruebas: Que Requieren las Solicitudes SEP por Perdida de Trabajo en Alabama

paragraphs.en: The healthcare.gov SEP application for Alabama job-loss situations requires documentation of the qualifying life event to validate the 60-day enrollment window. An Alabama employer termination letter with the date coverage ends is the most straightforward proof. If your Alabama employer's HR department provides a COBRA election notice, that document also confirms the qualifying event date and is accepted at healthcare.gov. A HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage, which Alabama employers covered by federal COBRA rules must provide within a reasonable time after coverage loss under Section 9831, details the type and dates of prior coverage and may be requested by a new employer for waiting-period waiver purposes.
paragraphs.es: La solicitud SEP de healthcare.gov para situaciones de perdida de trabajo en Alabama requiere documentacion del evento calificador de vida para validar la ventana de inscripcion de 60 dias. Una carta de terminacion del empleador de Alabama con la fecha en que termina la cobertura es la prueba mas directa. Si el departamento de recursos humanos de su empleador de Alabama proporciona un aviso de eleccion COBRA, ese documento tambien confirma la fecha del evento calificador y es aceptado en healthcare.gov. Un certificado de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA, que los empleadores de Alabama cubiertos por las reglas federales de COBRA deben proporcionar dentro de un tiempo razonable despues de la perdida de cobertura bajo la Seccion 9831, detalla el tipo y las fechas de cobertura anterior.

paragraphs.en: Income documentation for the Alabama Marketplace subsidy calculation follows IRS Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) rules. Alabama pay stubs from your final weeks of employment help establish your prior income. Your Alabama unemployment benefit award letter from the Alabama Department of Labor establishes your weekly benefit amount, which counts as income for ACA subsidy purposes. The healthcare.gov system will ask you to project your total 2026 income for the full year. If that projection later proves materially different from actual 2026 income, you reconcile at tax time using Form 1095-A and Schedule PTC. Underestimating income can lead to a tax-time repayment of excess advance premium tax credits; overestimating can lead to a tax refund. Keep all documentation from your Alabama employer and the Alabama Department of Labor unemployment agency in a secure location throughout the SEP process.
paragraphs.es: La documentacion de ingresos para el calculo del subsidio del Mercado de Alabama sigue las reglas del Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) del IRS. Los talones de pago de Alabama de sus ultimas semanas de empleo ayudan a establecer sus ingresos anteriores. Su carta de beneficio por desempleo de Alabama del Departamento de Trabajo de Alabama establece su monto de beneficio semanal, que cuenta como ingreso para propositos de subsidio ACA. El sistema de healthcare.gov le pedira que proyecte su ingreso total de 2026 para el ano completo. Si esa proyeccion luego resulta materialmente diferente del ingreso real de 2026, la reconcilia en el tiempo de impuestos usando el Formulario 1095-A y el Anexo PTC.

heading.en: 2026 ACA Subsidy Cliff and What It Means for Alabama Job-Loss Situations
heading.es: Precipicio del Subsidio ACA 2026 y Que Significa para las Perdidas de Trabajo en Alabama

paragraphs.en: The enhanced premium tax credits from the American Rescue Plan Act and the Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026. The 400% FPL subsidy cliff returned for plan year 2026. Alabama households with projected 2026 annual income above 400% FPL ($63,840 for a single person, $132,000 for a family of four) receive no premium tax credit under current law. For most Alabama residents who lose a job, however, the income drop moves them well below the 400% FPL cliff, making Marketplace subsidies available for the first time even if they were not subsidized while employed. ACA Marketplace Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions (CSR) are available only to Alabama households between 100% and 250% FPL. CSR plans reduce deductibles, copays, and out-of-pocket maximums significantly. The 2026 ACA Marketplace out-of-pocket maximum is $10,600 for an individual and $21,200 for a family per the HHS June 2025 NBPP revision. CSR plans for Alabama households under 150% FPL can reduce those maximums to as low as $3,000 individual and $6,000 family, per the CMS 2026 cost-sharing reduction schedule.
paragraphs.es: Los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados de la Ley del Plan de Rescate Americano y la Ley de Reduccion de Inflacion expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026. El precipicio de subsidio del 400% FPL regreso para el ano del plan 2026. Los hogares de Alabama con ingreso anual proyectado de 2026 sobre el 400% FPL ($63,840 para una persona, $132,000 para una familia de cuatro) no reciben credito fiscal de prima bajo la ley actual. Para la mayoria de residentes de Alabama que pierden un trabajo, sin embargo, la caida de ingresos los mueve muy por debajo del precipicio del 400% FPL, haciendo los subsidios del Mercado disponibles por primera vez. Los planes Silver del Mercado ACA con reducciones de costos compartidos (CSR) estan disponibles solo para hogares de Alabama entre 100% y 250% FPL. El maximo de gasto de bolsillo del Mercado ACA 2026 es $10,600 para un individuo y $21,200 para una familia por la revision NBPP de HHS de junio de 2025.

en.question: What is the Special Enrollment Period window after losing a job in Alabama in 2026?
en.answer: Your loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period in Alabama starts the day after your employer health coverage ends and runs for 60 consecutive calendar days. For example, if your last day of Alabama employer coverage is July 31, 2026, your SEP window runs August 1 through September 29, 2026. Apply and select a plan at healthcare.gov before Day 60. Plans take effect on the first of the month following enrollment. Alabama uses the federal healthcare.gov platform, not a state-based exchange. Medicaid has no deadline for those who qualify, but most Alabama job-loss situations do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid.

en.question: Does Alabama Medicaid cover you after losing a job?
en.answer: In most cases, no. Alabama is a non-expansion state and did not expand Medicaid under the ACA. Working-age adults in Alabama who are not pregnant, not parenting a minor child at very low income (typically under 18% FPL for parents), and do not have a Social Security Administration disability determination do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid regardless of income level. This means most Alabama residents who lose their jobs will not qualify for state Medicaid even if they have zero income. The primary coverage path for most Alabama job-loss situations is an ACA Marketplace SEP at healthcare.gov with income-based premium tax credits.

en.question: What is the Alabama coverage gap and who falls into it?
en.answer: The Alabama coverage gap affects adults whose projected 2026 income falls below 100% FPL ($15,060 for a single person, $31,200 for a family of four). Below 100% FPL in Alabama means you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid as a non-disabled, non-parenting adult, and you also do not qualify for ACA Marketplace premium tax credits, which start at 100% FPL. The gap exists because Alabama chose not to expand Medicaid, and federal law assumed expansion states would cover those below 100% FPL. If you project 2026 income in this range after job loss, consult the Alabama Medicaid Agency at medicaid.alabama.gov and a local health navigator for options including community health centers (FQHCs) that offer sliding-scale fees.

en.question: What documents do I need to apply for the SEP at healthcare.gov in Alabama?
en.answer: Healthcare.gov accepts your Alabama employer termination letter, a COBRA election notice, or a HIPAA certificate of creditable coverage as documentation of the qualifying life event. The document must show the date your Alabama employer coverage ends. Upload the document when starting your SEP application. If you do not have it yet, you can begin the application and upload later, but the 60-day SEP clock continues running from your coverage loss date. Contact your former Alabama employer's HR department immediately to request the termination letter and HIPAA certificate in writing.

en.question: Is COBRA worth it after losing a job in Alabama in 2026?
en.answer: COBRA is rarely the best financial choice after an Alabama job loss. Federal COBRA charges 102% of the full group premium, meaning you pay both the employer and employee share plus a 2% administrative fee. For an Alabama individual plan in 2026, that typically runs $500 to $900 per month; for family coverage, $1,200 to $2,800 per month. ACA Marketplace plans with income-based premium tax credits at healthcare.gov typically cost $10 to $300 per month for Alabama applicants with projected income between 100% and 400% FPL. COBRA makes sense mainly if you have ongoing treatment with an Alabama specialist not in any Marketplace network, or if your 2026 deductible is already substantially met. Alabama has no state mini-COBRA, so only federal COBRA applies, covering only employers with 20 or more employees.

en.question: Does unemployment income count toward ACA subsidy eligibility in Alabama?
en.answer: Yes. Alabama unemployment compensation counts as income for ACA Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) calculations at healthcare.gov. Include your weekly Alabama unemployment benefit multiplied by the number of weeks you expect to receive it in your projected 2026 annual income. This matters for two reasons specific to Alabama: first, it can push income above the 100% FPL coverage gap threshold, making you newly eligible for Marketplace premium tax credits; second, overestimating income could shift projected income above a subsidy bracket. An accurate projection reduces the risk of owing back advance premium tax credits at tax time using Form 1095-A.

en.question: What happens to my children's coverage after I lose my job in Alabama?
en.answer: Alabama's ALL Kids program (the state CHIP program) covers children up to age 19 in households with income up to 312% FPL (about $101,000 for a family of four in 2026), regardless of Medicaid expansion status. ALL Kids enrollment is open year-round with no deadline. Even if you do not qualify for Alabama Medicaid and fall into the Alabama coverage gap yourself, your children may qualify for ALL Kids at low or no cost. Apply through the Alabama Medicaid Agency at medicaid.alabama.gov or through healthcare.gov, which routes CHIP applications to the appropriate state program automatically.

en.question: What if I miss the 60-day SEP after losing my job in Alabama?
en.answer: Missing the 60-day loss-of-coverage SEP in Alabama means you typically cannot enroll in a subsidized Marketplace plan until the 2027 ACA Open Enrollment Period, which runs November 1 through January 15 for coverage starting January 1, 2027. Alabama Medicaid for most working-age adults remains unavailable regardless of the SEP deadline. If another qualifying life event occurs during the gap (moving to a new state, getting married, having a baby), that event restarts a new 60-day SEP. Short-term health plans are available outside SEP windows but are not ACA-compliant, do not cover pre-existing conditions, and carry significant coverage limitations and exclusions.

es.question: Cual es la ventana del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial despues de perder un trabajo en Alabama en 2026?
es.answer: Su Periodo de Inscripcion Especial por perdida de cobertura en Alabama comienza el dia despues de que termina su cobertura del empleador y dura 60 dias calendario consecutivos. Por ejemplo, si su ultimo dia de cobertura del empleador de Alabama es el 31 de julio de 2026, su ventana SEP corre del 1 de agosto al 29 de septiembre de 2026. Solicite y seleccione un plan en healthcare.gov antes del dia 60. Alabama usa la plataforma federal healthcare.gov, no un intercambio estatal. Medicaid no tiene fecha limite para quienes califican, pero la mayoria de perdidas de trabajo en Alabama no califican para Alabama Medicaid.

es.question: Cubre Alabama Medicaid despues de perder un trabajo?
es.answer: En la mayoria de casos, no. Alabama es un estado sin expansion y no expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA. Adultos en edad laboral en Alabama que no son embarazadas, no tienen hijos menores a ingresos muy bajos (tipicamente bajo el 18% FPL para padres), y no tienen una determinacion de discapacidad de la Administracion de Seguridad Social no califican para Alabama Medicaid independientemente del nivel de ingresos. La ruta de cobertura principal para la mayoria de perdidas de trabajo en Alabama es un SEP del Mercado ACA en healthcare.gov con creditos fiscales de prima basados en ingresos.

es.question: Que es la brecha de cobertura de Alabama y quien cae en ella?
es.answer: La brecha de cobertura de Alabama afecta a adultos cuyo ingreso proyectado de 2026 cae por debajo del 100% FPL ($15,060 para una persona, $31,200 para una familia de cuatro). Por debajo del 100% FPL en Alabama significa que no califica para Alabama Medicaid como adulto no discapacitado sin hijos, y tampoco califica para los creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado ACA, que comienzan en el 100% FPL. La brecha existe porque Alabama eligio no expandir Medicaid. Si proyecta ingresos de 2026 en este rango despues de perder el trabajo, consulte la Agencia de Medicaid de Alabama en medicaid.alabama.gov y un navegador de salud local para opciones.

es.question: Que documentos necesito para solicitar el SEP en healthcare.gov en Alabama?
es.answer: Healthcare.gov acepta su carta de terminacion del empleador de Alabama, un aviso de eleccion COBRA, o un certificado de cobertura acreditable de HIPAA como documentacion del evento calificador de vida. El documento debe mostrar la fecha en que termina su cobertura del empleador de Alabama. Cargue el documento cuando comience su solicitud SEP. Si aun no lo tiene, puede comenzar la solicitud y cargarlo despues, pero el reloj SEP de 60 dias sigue corriendo desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura. Contacte inmediatamente a los recursos humanos de su antiguo empleador de Alabama para solicitar la carta de terminacion y el certificado HIPAA por escrito.

es.question: Vale la pena COBRA despues de perder un trabajo en Alabama en 2026?
es.answer: COBRA raramente es la mejor opcion financiera despues de perder un trabajo en Alabama. El COBRA federal cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa, lo que significa que paga tanto la parte del empleador como la del empleado mas una tarifa administrativa del 2%. Para un plan individual en Alabama en 2026, eso tipicamente alcanza $500 a $900 al mes; para cobertura familiar, $1,200 a $2,800 al mes. Los planes del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales basados en ingresos en healthcare.gov tipicamente cuestan $10 a $300 al mes. COBRA tiene sentido principalmente si tiene tratamiento continuo con un especialista de Alabama que no esta en ninguna red del Mercado. Alabama no tiene COBRA estatal, por lo que solo aplica el COBRA federal, que cubre solo empleadores con 20 o mas empleados.

es.question: Cuenta el ingreso por desempleo para la elegibilidad de subsidio ACA en Alabama?
es.answer: Si. La compensacion por desempleo de Alabama cuenta como ingreso para los calculos del Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) del ACA en healthcare.gov. Incluya su beneficio semanal de desempleo de Alabama multiplicado por el numero de semanas que espera recibirlo en su ingreso anual proyectado de 2026. Esto importa por dos razones especificas para Alabama: primero, puede empujar los ingresos por encima del umbral del 100% FPL de la brecha de cobertura, haciendolo elegible para creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado; segundo, sobreestimar los ingresos podria desplazar el ingreso proyectado fuera de un tramo de subsidio.

es.question: Que pasa con la cobertura de mis hijos despues de perder mi trabajo en Alabama?
es.answer: El programa ALL Kids de Alabama (el programa CHIP estatal) cubre ninos hasta los 19 anos en hogares con ingresos hasta el 312% FPL (alrededor de $101,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026), independientemente del estado de expansion de Medicaid. La inscripcion de ALL Kids es abierta todo el ano sin fecha limite. Incluso si no califica para Alabama Medicaid y cae en la brecha de cobertura de Alabama, sus hijos pueden calificar para ALL Kids a bajo costo o sin costo. Solicite a traves de la Agencia de Medicaid de Alabama en medicaid.alabama.gov o a traves de healthcare.gov, que enruta solicitudes CHIP al programa estatal correspondiente automaticamente.

es.question: Que pasa si pierdo el SEP de 60 dias despues de perder mi trabajo en Alabama?
es.answer: Perder el SEP de 60 dias por perdida de cobertura en Alabama significa que tipicamente no puede inscribirse en un plan del Mercado subsidiado hasta el Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta del ACA 2027, que corre del 1 de noviembre al 15 de enero para cobertura del 1 de enero de 2027. Alabama Medicaid para la mayoria de adultos en edad laboral sigue sin disponibilidad independientemente del plazo SEP. Si ocurre otro evento calificador de vida durante la brecha (mudarse a un nuevo estado, casarse, tener un bebe), ese evento reinicia un nuevo SEP de 60 dias. Los planes de salud a corto plazo estan disponibles fuera de las ventanas SEP pero no son compatibles con el ACA y no cubren condiciones preexistentes.
